newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks ease in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks ease in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were weak in Monday morning trade, with analysts expecting a consolidation ahead of the Friday's U.S. employment data and the U.S. presidential election.
The Hang Seng index was down 14.62 points at 12,373.76. Turnover was HK$1.38 billion after the first 50 minutes of trade.
"There is some selling pressure in the property sector. For the last two months the property counters led the market," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
The Hang Seng properties sub-index was down 175 points at 23,352.
Analysts said a fall in Henderson Land shares exaggerated the Hang Seng's movement. The stock went ex-dividend on Monday and was down HK$0.57 at HK$68.25.
"I guess the market seems to be losing a bit of momentum," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities (HK) Ltd.

He said after the market's run to new record levels, investors had been reluctant to take profits. However, weakness over the last two sessions may have encouraged more investors to lock in gains. "Once they saw there was not so much upside momentum, some started to take a bit of profit," Tsang said.
Chia said the Hang Seng could remain in a range of 12,300 to 12,600 points this week.
"This Friday we have (U.S.) payroll figures and next week is the U.S. presidential elections so maybe until then you will see a consolidation for Hong Kong and also U.S. markets," he said.
Tsang agreed. "This might continue until the U.S. presidential election. Before that, I don't think there will be a major movement or big upside movements for the U.S. market," he said.
October Hang Seng futures, which expire on Wednesday, rose three points to 12,383.

Shares in New World Development rose HK$0.50 to HK$44.20. Companion Building Material has reached a conditional agreement to buy New World's Super Trend unit in a HK$70.4 million share swap. Companion Building shares were down HK$0.01 at HK$1.48.
Shares in China Treasure resumed trading on Monday and fell HK$0.07 to HK$0.21. The company announced a HK$104 million one-for-one rights issue at HK$0.17 per share.
